clauses.text: Approved  Code  No.   119 CODE  OF  FAIR  COMPETITION FOR  THE NEWSPRINT  INDUSTRY As  Approved  on  November  17,  1933 BY PRESIDENT  ROOSEVELT Executive     Order An  application  having  been  duly  made,  pursuant  to  and  in  full compliance  with  the  provisions  of  Title  I  of  the  National  Industrial Recovery  Act,  approved  June  16,  1933,  for  my  approval  of  a  Code  of Fair  Competition  of  the  Newsprint  Industry,  and  hearings  having been  held  thereon  and  the  Administrator  having  rendered  his  report containing  an  analysis  of  the  said  Code  of  Fair  Competition  together with  his  recommendations  and  findings  with  respect  thereto,  and  the Administrator  having  found  that  tlie  said  Code  of  Fair  Competition complies  in  all  respects  with  the  pertinent  provisions  of  Title  I  of said  Act  and  that  the  requirements  of  clauses  (1)  and  (2)  of  subsec- tion (a)  of  Section  3  of  the  said  Act  have  been  met: NOW,  THEREFORE,  I,  Franklin  D.  Roosevelt,  President  of  the United  States,  pursuant  to  the  authority  vested  in  me  by  Title  I  of the  National  Industrial  Recovery  Act,  approved  June  16,  1933,  and otherwise,  do  adopt  and  approve  the  report,  recommendations,  and findings  of  the  Administrator  and  do  order  that  the  said  Code  of Fair  Competition  be  and  it  is  hereby  approved,  however,  feeling that  the  minimum  wage  for  this  industry  should  be  not  less  than forty  (40)  cents  per  hour,  my  order  of  approval  is  subject  to  the following  condition : That  within  90  days  from  the  effective  date  of  this  Code  the Administrator  hold  such  further  hearing  upon  such  notice  as  he, in  his  discretion,  shall  fix  for  the  purpose  of  determining  the  adequacy of  the  minimum  wages  established  in  said  Code,  after  which  his report  and  recommendation  shall  be  submitted  to  me  for  further  order which  order  shall  have  the  effect  of  a  condition  to  my  approval  of this  Code. FRANKLIN  D.  ROOSEVELT. Approval  recommended : Hugh  S.  Johnson, Administrator. The  White  House, November  17,  1933. 29225" 29&-95 34  (103)

Identity and page check: the held text for EO 6437 is the American Presidency Project transcription (APP node 362263), registered as grade mirror_transcription (not an original). Its page record is a Common Crawl capture of 2025-01-23T04:06:53Z whose heading names Executive Order 6437, whose date (November 17, 1933) and subject agree with the text, and whose text sha256 equals the held text's. The WPA 1944 list row (1933 Nov 17 p.551: Code of Fair Competition for the Paper and Pulp In dustry approved. III NRA Codes 115 ; I NRA Hand Supp 215.) confirms the order's date and subject. The order approves a code of fair competition under section 3(a) of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, so the reviewed shared analysis (SHARED_ANALYSIS.md and review-shared/ADJUDICATION.json) applies: a code-dependent command that did not end earlier ended on June 14, 1935 by statutory repeal (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2); Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization, not an end date. The machine inventory had one clause covering both the approval and the condition; it is corrected into two clauses (the approval, and the hearing-and-report condition) so each command has its own end.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The approval is \"subject to the following condition\", a hearing-and-report requirement measured from the code's effective date; the order states no period for the approval itself and no \"until\" date or provisional approval. Searched the held order texts (jobs/*/output/texts, through the Cruden lookup and a follow-up regex search on the code's name), the census register and the WPA 1944 list for later orders citing EO 6437 by number or naming its code: no held order text cites EO 6437 by number. EO 6964-B (February 5, 1935) amends Article V of this code on \"upon the report and recommendation and findings of the National Industrial Recovery Board with respect to the adequacy of the minimum wages established in the Code of Fair Competition for the Paper and Pulp Industry as approved by me on November 17, 1933\", and orders that \"the previous approval of said Code is hereby amended to include an approval of said Code in its entirety as amended\". It amends and re-approves the code, so it is a later event, not an end. It also bears on condition (2) below: it appears to be the further order that followed a report on the adequacy of the minimum wages, but it does not say it discharges this condition, and no held text records the hearing or its date. No held record shows this code cancelled, modified under section 10(b), superseded, revoked or suspended before June 14, 1935. June 16, 1935 is not an end: section 1 of S.J. Res. 113 replaced the original two-year expiry with April 1, 1936.","independent_command_check":"The order states that \"my order of approval is subject to the following condition\" and then directs, as the condition, that \"within 90 days from the effective date of this code the Administrator hold such further hearing upon such notice as he, in his discretion, shall fix for the purpose of determining the adequacy of the minimum wages established in said code\", after which \"his report and recommendation shall be submitted to me for further order, which order shall have the effect of a condition to my approval of this code\". The direction to the Administrator is part of the condition of approval that section 3(a) of Title I permits (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA3: conditions \"as a condition of his approval of any such code\", including reporting requirements), and its further order would operate only \"as a condition\" of the approval; the order cites only Title I and the general words \"and otherwise\", so it is not an appointment or delegation under another statute. The 90 days run from the code's effective date, which no held source states, and a report or hearing deadline is not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21, report deadline), so the claim computes no end from it and records no performance date.","savings_check":"Savings reviewed under NIRA section 5 and S.J. Res. 113 section 2 and its proviso: accrued acts, liabilities and any completed-action exemption under the Code of Fair Competition of the Paper and Pulp Industry are preserved as accrued effects; nothing continues the approval, and no held source shows a prosecution or enforcement continued after June 14, 1935.","scope_check":"Two clauses after correction: the approval of the Code of Fair Competition of the Paper and Pulp Industry (chars 727-1257) and the hearing-and-report condition (chars 1259-1667). The order states no other condition, exception, stay or exemption."}

savings_residuals.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the approved Code of Fair Competition of the Paper and Pulp Industry before June 14, 1935 are accrued consequences that the repeal did not turn into continuing commands; nothing in S.J. Res. 113 (SUPPLEMENT:SJRES113) continues the approval after June 14, 1935. Any antitrust exemption for complying action before the repeal (NIRA section 5, SUPPLEMENT:NIRA5) is likewise an accrued effect; the resolution's proviso, which extends the exemption only to "agreements and action thereunder" meeting stated conditions, leaves open how far it narrowed the exemption for past action, so the claim records no continuing exemption and no surviving approval. Any hearing held, report made or further order issued under the condition before the repeal is an accrued act, not a continuing command.
